entities.summary:
Nissan Motor Company, founded in 1933 in Yokohama, Japan, is one of Japan's three largest automakers and part of the Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi Alliance — the world's largest automotive group by vehicle sales. Nissan's history encompasses Japanese industrial militarism (producing wartime vehicles), post-war recovery, American market conquest with fuel-efficient small cars during the 1970s oil crisis, Carlos Ghosn's rescue and fraud scandal, and the electric vehicle revolution led by the Nissan Leaf.

Nissan was established from the Jidosha-Seizo company in 1933 under Yoshisuke Aikawa's Nissan zaibatsu. Post-war, Nissan grew through American market exports — the Datsun brand (renamed Nissan in 1981) offered fuel-efficient small cars precisely when the 1973 oil crisis made American large cars undesirable. By 1981, Nissan was producing 3 million vehicles annually.

Carlos Ghosn, dispatched by Renault to rescue the bankrupt Nissan in 1999, implemented drastic cost cuts (closing 5 factories, eliminating 21,000 jobs) that returned Nissan to profitability and created the Renault-Nissan Alliance. Ghosn's 2018 arrest in Japan for financial misconduct and his 2019 dramatic escape from house arrest hidden in a music equipment case to Lebanon became one of the most extraordinary business crime stories in history. Nissan's Leaf (2010) was the world's first mass-market pure electric car.
